proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 2 (Gamma_A = range J_A), 3 (Gram operator is a unit) and 4 (projection formula), stated for an arbitrary parametrization J of the graph and an arbitrary transpose T of J.

1. J is injective. Suppose J v = J v'. Then graphPoint v (A v) = graphPoint v' (A v'). By definition graphPoint x y = toLp 2 (Fin.append x y), so for i in Fin n its coordinate at the index Fin.castAdd l i is x_i (Fin.append_left). Comparing these coordinates gives v_i = v'_i for all i, hence v = v'.

2. T o J has trivial kernel. Let v satisfy T(J v) = 0. Applying the hypothesis on T with w = J v gives ||J v||^2 = <J v, J v> = <T(J v), v> = <0, v> = 0, so J v = 0 = J 0 and v = 0 by step 1.

3. T o J is a unit. R^n is finite-dimensional, so a linear endomorphism of R^n with trivial kernel is a unit of the linear endomorphisms (LinearMap.isUnit_iff_ker_eq_bot); for continuous linear endomorphisms of the complete space R^n this is equivalent to being a unit of L(R^n, R^n) (ContinuousLinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_toLinearMap). With step 2 this proves IsUnit (T o J), the first conclusion. Put R := Ring.inverse(T o J); since T o J is a unit, (T o J) o R = 1 (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel), i.e. T(J(R u)) = u for every u in R^n.

4. Gamma_A = range J. By the hypothesis on J, the generating set {graphPoint v (A v) : v in R^n} equals Set.range J. The range of the linear map J is a submodule whose underlying set is Set.range J (LinearMap.coe_range), and the span of a submodule is itself (Submodule.span_eq). Hence Gamma_A = range J; in particular every z in Gamma_A has the form z = J v.

5. Orthogonality. Fix w in R^(n+l) and put p := J(R(T w)) = (J o (R o T)) w. Then p is in range J = Gamma_A. For z = J v in Gamma_A, using the hypothesis on T twice (with w and with J(R(T w))) and step 3:
 <w - p, J v> = <w, J v> - <J(R(T w)), J v> = <T w, v> - <T(J(R(T w))), v> = <T w, v> - <T w, v> = 0.

6. Conclusion. Gamma_A is a finite-dimensional, hence complete, subspace, so it has an orthogonal projection, and by its characterization (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero: if p is in K and <w - p, z> = 0 for all z in K, then K.starProjection w = p) we get starProjection_(Gamma_A) w = (J o (R o T)) w. Since w is arbitrary, starProjection_(Gamma_A) = J o (Ring.inverse(T o J) o T) (ext), the second conclusion.
key_steps: J is injective (castAdd coordinates of graphPoint v (A v) are v_i)
ker(T o J) = 0 since <T J v, v> = ||J v||^2; finite dimension makes T o J a unit of L(R^n, R^n)
w - J R T w is orthogonal to every J v because T J R = 1
eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero identifies starProjection with J o Ring.inverse(T o J) o T
